slides.title: Why your blades wash out in corners
slides.sub: Sharpen short track blades the right way

slides.title: The jig matters more than the stone
slides.body: A stone can only follow the surface it is given. A blade clamped slightly twisted gets a taper that grips at the front and washes out at the back.

slides.title: Three edges, seen end on
slides.caption: Sharpening turns a rounded or burred edge back into a flat bottom with two crisp corners.

slides.title: Save the coarse side
slides.body: Use it only for a nick, a rust pit or a corner gone round. Most sessions belong on the fine side, with long, even passes.

slides.title: Always remove the burr
slides.body: Sharpening leaves a thin lip of steel that feels sharp and folds on the ice. A few light passes with a diamond deburr stone on both sides take it off.

slides.title: Polish for glide
slides.body: Sharpening gives you grip. Polishing gives you glide. Work the triangle from blue to green to pink until the gliding surface is a clean mirror.

slides.title: Look for a bright line
slides.body: A dull edge reflects a bright line. A truly sharp edge reflects nothing back. Any bright spot is a flat you have not reached yet.
